4. Plaint case in short, inter alia. is that Abdul Jobbar Sheikh and Moyez Ali Bepari were the owner in possession of the suit property and ROR khatian No.98 was prepared in their names. By way of an amicable family arrangement, the suit property included in the shaham of Moyez Ali Bepari. Subsequently Moyez Ali Bepari transferred the said land in favour of Sukur Mahmud through registered sale deed dated 02.11.1960. Thereafter the plaintiff purchased the suit property from the said Sukur Mahmud by registered sale deed No.18635 dated 07.12.1960. Thereby the plaintiff became owner and possessor of the suit land and remained in possession after mutating his name and paying rent to the government. On 02.03.2007 the defendant Nos.2, 3 and 4 entering into the suit property denied the right and title of the plaintiff and claimed that the government has taken the property as khas land and threatened to evict the plaintiff from the suit property and to demolish his house thereafter, although government has no right and title over the suit property. Since thus plaintiff's title became clouded he filed the suit. 

 5. The defendants-government contested the suit by filing written statement, denying the plaint case, alleging, inter alia that the suit land is situated within the bazaar named as Dagla Bazar. Government acquired the property and thereafter leased the same to different persons as yearly basis and in the latest survey the suit property has recorded in the khas khatian and thereafter asked the illegal occupant to evict from the suit property. The plaintiff did neither have any title, nor any possession of the suit land. The suit is false and is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 15. In support of the contention of the government, one Humayun Kabir,. Union Panshad Assistant Land Officer deposed in Court as DW.1 who has' simply asserted the claim of the government, saying that it was recorded in the name of the government as khas khattan No.l. Although in support of the government claimed to the effect that the property was included in the but bazar as well as acquired by the government and leased if oat to any persons, nothing was produced in Cow. Surprising to notice that DWI I' admitted in his cross-examination by the plaintiff that: “নালিশী ভূমির আর ও আর আঃ জব্বার ও ময়েজউদ্দিন ব্যাপারীর নাম।-----------আর ও আর ৯৮নং খতিয়ানের আংশিক যে অংশ বাজারে পড়ে নাই সেখানই নালিশী জমি।” 

 This statement of fact proved about of his being out of sense. Since the property has been claimed by the government as a khas land and tried to lease it out. Which is the main cause of action of the suit for which the plaintiff filed the suit. By saying the above statement PW.I did not admits the fact that the suit property went within the bazar- rather he wanted to say that by claiming the suit property as khas land, government is now trying to lease out as well as Mr. which he was constrained to file the suit. From a managed about 90 years old, it cannot be expected more then this one. The above quotation as held by the Courts below is nothing but a misreading of the evidence. When the plaintiff case has been proved by adducing sufficient witness as well as his title and possession was legally been proved and defendant witness by way of admission proved the plaintiffs case; the Courts-below committed illegality in not giving the decree in favour of the plaintiff. Accordingly, I found merit in this rule.
